vulnerablePath: POST /rest/v1/rpc/search_invoices with the public anon key (or GET /api/invoices/search?q=...)
public.search_invoices() glues p_customer into the statement text and runs it with RETURN QUERY EXECUTE
SECURITY DEFINER: the invoice policies do not apply, so `%' or true --` drops the tenant filter
expectedSecureBehavior: The search text only ever matches customer names: a quote in it is a literal character, anonymous callers are refused, and no search returns another tenant's invoices.
acceptableFixes: Pass the search text with EXECUTE ... USING (or write the query without EXECUTE), with SECURITY INVOKER so the invoice policies still apply
Quote the value with format('%L') or quote_literal() and keep the tenant filter; revoke EXECUTE from anon
unacceptableFixes: Stripping or escaping quotes in the route handler while the function stays callable straight through PostgREST
Revoking anon only: any signed-in user can still read every tenant's invoices with the same input
Switching to SECURITY INVOKER while still gluing the text in: RLS then limits the damage, but the caller still writes the SQL
